newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - high, low sulphur gap widens.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - high, low sulphur gap widens.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil was weaker on Thursday while low sulphur prices rose again, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $86 fob ARA and ended the day at around $86/$87, after having earlier ranged above those levels.

High sulphur cargoes were weaker, as a U.K. utility bought a 20-25,000 tonne cargo, for delivery approximately in the first 20 days of March, at $85 cif NWE. This set a distinctly lower tone for the market, as offers had earlier been seen closer to $88/$89.
Other high sulphur material was also seen available.
Low sulphur fuel, however, was slightly stronger.

Dealers noted some end user interest from Italy for the second half of March and said the latest Turkish tender for 60-65,000 tonnes of low sulphur fuel oil, for delivery into Izmir and Izmit in late March, added a layer of support.
A Spanish refiner was also seen having fixed a 30,000 tonne vessel from Scandinavia to the Canaries in the first week of March, and this was expected to contain low sulphur fuel oil.
Swaps were firmer and talked at around $96/$97 fob NWE for March.
